summary: In this excerpt from a fiction book (Book 6, part 77), the narrator is captured by a group of armed men and placed in a van, handcuffed to the door. Inside sits a middle-aged man called the Lancer, who fiddles with meditation balls and questions the narrator about why people are after him. The narrator admits to helping Halliday with her proof, then claims the NSA tried to recruit him and that he refused, hoping to pass as a helpless street mathematician. The Lancer, unconvinced, offers him a deal: help them or be spared death.
one_line: A captured mathematician bluffs his way through an interrogation by the enigmatic Lancer, who offers a deal to save his life.
key_facts: The narrator pretends to be a helpless street mathematician after being captured.
Captors take the gun the narrator stole from a DHS agent, along with his burner cell phone and other pockets' contents.
The narrator is handcuffed to the door of a van, which is one of many vans and SUVs the captors own.
The Lancer is a middle-aged, long-faced, lantern-jawed man with bronze skin, greasy brown hair around a bald spot, and hair falling to his shoulders.
The Lancer clacks a set of meditation balls in one hand and keeps an intricately carved walking stick by his knee.
The narrator admits to the Lancer that he helped Halliday with her proof.
The narrator says 'it wasn't worth it' when describing helping Halliday with her proof.
The narrator asks the Lancer 'Are you the Lancer?' and the meditation balls stop, signaling the Lancer's alarm.
The narrator claims the NSA tried to grab him because they thought he was working for the Lancer.
The Lancer says 'I have many names' and mocks the United States National Security Agency as having stupid games.
The narrator says the NSA tried to offer him a deal and that he refused because 'They weren't offering enough.'
The Lancer offers the narrator a deal: help them, and 'we won't kill you.'
